verdict.rationale: Azure documents its own client libraries: most service REST APIs have them, and an SDK lifecycle policy covers client libraries with 12 months' notice before retiring an SDK. The evidence is thin, though, and says coverage is "most" services rather than all. Missing for 10: the languages and package names supported, SDK install or getting-started docs, coverage of every service, and independent or hands-on corroboration of building against the SDKs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Most Azure service REST APIs have client libraries that provide a native interface for using Azure services

The Microsoft Azure SDK policy covers Microsoft Azure SDK authoring tools, REST APIs, client libraries, command-line utilities, compute & storage emulators, and Azure Tools for Microsoft Visual Studio
